handbookNote: New Jersey State Police Marine Services Bureau (NJSP MSB) Boat Safety Certificate program -- unlike most states, New Jersey's certificate requirement is NOT birth-date-gated: it applies to anyone operating a power vessel or PWC on NJ waters, and NJ is one of the few states requiring a two-step process -- a NASBLA-approved course (online, e.g. boat-ed.com/newjersey, AceBoater, BOATERexam, Recademics, or classroom) PLUS a mandatory in-person, proctored exam at an approved test site before the permanent certificate is issued (bring course completion certificate + photo ID); the online course itself requires 70% on unit quizzes and 80% on its final exam with unlimited attempts (confirmed live 2026 on NJSP MSB FAQ and boat-ed.com/newjersey), while the separate in-person exam's own question count/passing score is not publicly published by NJSP and is hedged accordingly; PWC operation is flatly barred under 16 even with a certificate, 13-15 year olds are limited to electric-motor or under-10-hp 12ft+ vessels; registration/titling is handled by the NJ Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) rather than a wildlife agency; NJ's own minimum-headway-speed (no-wake) rule applies within 200 feet of docks/piers/marinas and in waterways/bridge openings under 200/400 feet -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
